test_title: SSC CGL 2021 Tier-I (Held On : 20 April 2022 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Which of the following Amendments of the Constitution of India amended Article 19 and inserted provisions fully securing the constitutional validity of zamindari abolition laws in general and certain specified State Acts in particular?
solution:
The correct answer is __**First Amendment**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The first amendment of** **the **Indian Constitution was done in 1951**.
 
• Constitution (**First Amendment) Act, 1951 amended Articles 15, 19, 85, 87, 174, 176, 341, 342, 372 and 376.**
 
• Nehru administration made a** provision limiting Article 19(1)(a) of the Constitution of India against "abuse of freedom of speech and expression.**
 
• ​The** right of citizens of India to practice any profession or to carry on any occupation, trade, or business conferred by article 19(1)(g)** is subject to reasonable restrictions that the laws of the State may impose, in the interests of the general public.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• There is a total of **106 amendments **made in the Indian constitution, till now.
 
• The provision for amendments is given in **article 368 of the Indian Constitution**.
 
• **Dr . Bhimrao Ramji Ambedkar** is known as the father of the Indian Constitution.
 
• **42nd amendment** is also known as** the mini-constitution of India**.
 
• Amendments in our I**ndian constitution are adopted** from the constitution of **South Africa**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
 

 **Amendments**
 **Year**
 **What was done**
 
 

 **1st**
 **1951**
 
 
 
• ​Empowerment of state to make special provisions for economically backward class.
 
• Added article 19(1)(a), 19 (1)(g), 31A, 31B, 341, 342, 15(3), 46, 341, 342, 372, 376
 
• Saving of law for acquisition of estates.
 
• 3 more grounds for restriction on speech.
 
 
 
 

 **2nd**
 **1952**
 
 
 
• Readjusting the scale of representation in Lok sabha.
 
 
 
 

 **3rd**
 **1954**
 
 
 
• Empowering the parliament to control the production supply and distribution of foodstuff, cattle fodder cotton, jute, etc.
 
 
 
 

 **4th**
 **1955**
 
 
 
• The scale of compensation for acquisition of property
 
• Authorize the state to nationalize any trade.
 
• Included some more action in the ninth schedule.
 
• Extended the scope of Article 31A
 
 
 
 

d9:T
